title: Physical Intelligence Opens Pi API Beta for Robot Foundation Models
source_used: Physical Intelligence announcement 'Frontier Models for Every Robot: Announcing our API beta' (pi.website/blog/api-beta), plus Unite.AI (read in full)
key_facts: Physical Intelligence announced the Pi API beta on 13 Oct 2026, giving outside developers hosted fine-tuning and inference on its latest robot foundation models.

Workflow: a developer uploads robot data, launches fine-tuning on compute the company manages, and runs the fine-tuned model on a robot through a hosted gateway; evaluation data guides the next round.
Access to the beta is through a waitlist; applicants describe what they want to build.
Actor, a Utah company, showed an autonomous wheel loader scooping material into a dump truck with no operator inside, in footage described as a real commercial deployment.
Almond, based in San Francisco, builds Axol, a dual-arm robot; Axol deburred spacers used in its own assembly while running a model obtained after four days of iterating with the Pi API.
Most examples ran on cloud-hosted inference in Japan, Switzerland and the United States; the company noted areas for improvement, including network connectivity problems for some.
The company calls the effort still early and says developer feedback will shape future releases.
quote_evidence: Physical Intelligence announced the Pi API beta on October 13, 2026, making its latest robotic foundation models available to outside developers for hosted fine-tuning and inference.
Access to the beta runs through a waitlist, with applicants asked to describe what they want to build.
The company said these early deployments covered a range of environments and tasks and highlighted areas for improvement, including network connectivity challenges for some.
why_it_matters_hint: Robot makers can adapt a ready-made robot AI model without building their own training setup.
notes: Pool item was Unite.AI, whose article (AI-generated, per its own byline note) restates the company announcement; I read the original at pi.website and credit Physical Intelligence as the first reporter. Demonstrations are the company's own footage.
